ei.title: Chapter 5-16 3번: Evolution: Not Perfection but Satisficing
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: One common misunderstanding of evolution is that it leads inexorably to organisms that are ever better designed. But Darwinian evolution is not a process of perfection. In contrast to the Lamarckian and Great Chain of Being theories of evolution, natural selection does not inexorably drive species up some kind of ladder of perfection. Rather, natural selection is, to borrow a term from economics, a process that leads to satisficing (just being "good enough for now"). In other words, so long as you survive and do better than your rivals, that is good enough. An antelope does not have to become the fastest animal on earth; it simply has to be faster than the lions that try to catch it. By the same token, lions and other predators do not have to be able to run marathons at top speed; nor do they have to be able to catch every prey animal. They just have to be fast enough to catch sufficient prey animals to survive.

questions.passage: One (A)[rare / common] misunderstanding of evolution is that it leads inexorably to organisms that are ever (B)[better / worse] designed. But Darwinian evolution is not a process of (C)[perfection / mediocrity]. In contrast to the Lamarckian and Great Chain of Being theories of evolution, natural selection does not inexorably drive species up some kind of ladder of perfection. Rather, natural selection is, to borrow a term from economics, a process that leads to satisficing (just being "good enough for now"). In other words, so long as you survive and do better than your rivals, that is good enough. An antelope does not have to become the fastest animal on earth; it simply has to be faster than the lions that try to catch it. By the same token, lions and other predators do not have to be able to run marathons at top speed; nor do they have to be able to catch every prey animal. They just have to be fast enough to catch sufficient prey animals to survive.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 흔한(common) 오해, 더 잘(better) 설계된 유기체, 완벽(perfection)의 과정이 아님.
det.analysis:
❌ ① rare (A 반대: 흔한→드문)
✅ ② common — better — perfection — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ worse (B 반대: 더 나은→더 나쁜)
❌ ④ mediocrity (C 반대: 완벽→평범함)
det.tip: common(흔한) ↔ rare(드문), better(더 나은) ↔ worse(더 나쁜)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 만족화로 이어지고(leads), 살아남으며(survive), 사자보다 더 빨라야(faster) 함.
det.analysis:
✅ ① leads — survive — faster — 원문 일치 ←정답

❌ ③ perish (B 반대: 살아남다→죽다)

questions.passage: One common misunderstanding of evolution is that it leads inexorably to organisms that are ever better designed. But Darwinian evolution is not a process of perfection. In contrast to the Lamarckian and Great Chain of Being theories of evolution, natural selection does not inexorably drive species up some kind of ladder of perfection. Rather, natural selection is, to borrow a term from economics, a process that leads to satisficing (just being "good enough for now"). In other words, so long as you survive and do better than your rivals, that is good enough. An antelope does not have to become the fastest animal on earth; it simply has to be faster than the lions that try to catch it. By the same token, lions and other predators do not have to be able to run marathons at top speed; nor do they have to be able to catch every prey animal. They just have to be __________ to survive.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
